paragraphs: Friend, look at who is talking in this passage. Laban's sons are talking, and Laban's face is talking, and none of it is friendly. Then the LORD speaks: "Go back to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you." (Genesis 31:3) When the room gets cold, the voice that counts is the One who says go, and who says He will be there.

Now watch what Jacob does with that. He doesn't keep it to himself, he calls Rachel and Leah out to the field and tells them what God has done, saying, "the God of my father has been with me." (Genesis 31:5) He can look back at ten changed wages and say God did not allow Laban to harm him (Genesis 31:7). I think that's a good habit for you, baker: stop and look back at where God has been with you.

But I won't pretend the ending is tidy. Rachel steals the household idols, and Jacob deceives Laban by not telling him he is running away (Genesis 31:19-20). Even people God is leading carry baggage out the door with them. God's promise holds anyway, and I'm so glad, because I show up with plenty of my own baggage, and He still pulled me out of a drawer.
